newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SURANYI-HUNGARY BGT PLAN STANDS DESPITE SOC.SEC GAP.
newsitem.headline: SURANYI-HUNGARY BGT PLAN STANDS DESPITE SOC.SEC GAP.

text.p: Hungary's central bank chairman Gyorgy Suranyi said Hungary would meet its 1997 budget deficit target despite a larger-than-planned social security deficit.

"I am concerned, but due to the fact that the central government budget performance is (above expectations) I don't see any slippage by the end of the year in the general government balances," Suranyi told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview broadcast on Thursday.

According to the latest figures, the social security deficit was 21.3 billion forints in March, well above the 13.5 billion forint targeted for the whole year, and official forecasts put it as much as 40 billion forints for the year.
The Finance Ministry said it was working on plans to reduce the deficit through improving the collection of social security and tax revenues.
Suranyi has said a persistently high social security deficit could put in question in the longer term the country's commitment to tight fiscal policies.
However he told RFTV that improvements in other areas of the budget would ensure that the overshoot would not endanger the overall budget deficit target of 4.9 percent of GDP.
"Even if the social security (deficit) might exceed the targeted level, the government borrowing repuirement will be in line with forecasts," he said.
